subject: Compact eval — hour-pool top-up vs short extension
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@novatel.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novatel.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — two options for our compact eval

Hi Soojin,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're wrapping up our compact eval next week and hit a small runway issue: our engineering team used more concurrent runtime than expected. We have two paths we can take and wanted to get your preference and a crisp price before we decide: 

1) Buy an hour-pool top-up (one-time) that the team can draw from over the next 3 weeks. Approx need: ~150 GPU hours.
2) Short extension: add 2 extra weeks to the evaluation window (same capacity), so we finish the last integration tests.

Which option would be cheaper for us? Is there any room for a modest discount given we're evaluating for an imminent pilot? I'm attaching a usage export so you can see the burst profile.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that's easier.

Alex
Senior ML Eng, Novatel AI
-- Attachment: usage-report_Q2.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alex Moreno <alex@novatel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novatel.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — two options for our compact eval

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the export, that helped. High-level: both are doable, but the economics and internal approvals differ. Quick summary below and a recommended path.

Option A — Hour-pool top-up
- One-time purchase of 150 GPU hours.
- Suggested list price: $28/hr (on your current config) => $4,200 before discounts.
- Benefit: immediate capacity, no contract amendment.
- Can convert unused hours to credits on your next purchase within 90 days.

Option B — 2-week extension
- Extend the time-boxed eval by 14 calendar days and keep the same hourly quota.
- Cost: flat extension fee that basically covers expected infra overage; estimate ~$3,200 (lower unit rate since we amortize baseline).
- Requires a short addendum to the SOW (legal + signature).

Recommendation: Hour-pool top-up for speed. If you need the calendar breathing room (e.g., stakeholder demos), the extension is cleaner.

Discounts: I can offer a 10% discretionary discount on the hour-pool if you commit to a pilot purchase conversation within 30 days (we'll capture in HubSpot). For an extension, I can escalate to Ben for a manager approval to reach a similar price band.

If you’re aligned, I’ll draft an SOW addendum and a short invoice for the hour-pool. Want me to include the 10% contingent discount in the initial doc?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novatel.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — two options for our compact eval

Thanks Soojin,

Hour-pool sounds like the right move — immediate unblock for the team. Two follow-ups: 1) would Novatel be eligible for the 10% contingent discount if we get the PO in within 30 days? Yes. 2) In the event we don't use all 150 hours, what is the conversion rate to credits?

Also, we prefer a one-line invoice we can route to finance rather than a multi-page addendum if possible.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Appreciate the thread. Ben chiming in on the discount mechanics.

We can approve a one-time 10% discretionary discount on the 150-hour pool contingent on:
- Novatel scheduling a pilot scoping call (sales + engineering) within 30 days.
- A one-line PO or email confirmation from your procurement committing to the hour purchase.

Conversion for unused hours: 1 hour -> $26 credit (applied to next purchase within 90 days). That conversion is slightly better than list to encourage reuse.

Soojin — to keep it lightweight for Novatel, please prepare: 
- Short invoice (one page) for $3,780 (150 hrs @ $28/hr less 10% = $3,780).
- Simple payment instructions + PO line.
- SOW addendum only if they choose extension route.

Marissa — can you queue a PO-ready invoice in Stripe linked to DEAL-4721 and attach the SOW-draft to the HubSpot deal?

Thanks — Ben
